lessonTitle: African American Community Leaders in Florida
title: Hall of Florida Leaders
details: 📅 Q4 · Unit 11 · Civil Rights, Community Leaders, and Contemporary Florida

badge.name: Field Seal 26
badge.line: Only field historians earn this one. You went where your teacher can't go, and you brought back proof.

hook.look: A field file is a job card. It tells a historian where to go and what to bring back.
hook.head: Field File 26 · Hall of Florida Leaders
rows: A hall that honors five Florida leaders
Your teacher, still stuck inside Canvas
hook.alt: Three men in suits walk arm in arm at the front of a crowd with signs
hook.cap: A. Philip Randolph (middle) leads the March on Washington, August 28, 1963. U.S. National Archives.
hook.note: New name plates keep showing up on my wall. Can you build a hall with one object for each leader?

opti.brief: She can't leave Canvas, so you build it. Make a hall with one object for each of five leaders. Then send her one photo.
opti.desk: No headset? Use my desk. Play the game, then write 2 sentences for your teacher.

vr.look: A gallery is a big room for showing important things. Each object stands for what one leader did. No statues of people: the object tells the story.

models.name: Western Town Green Train
models.why: A. Philip Randolph: train workers' union

steps.title: Get ready
steps.html:
These are the models you will use. In VR, type the gray word in the Models search box to find each one.

@MODELS@

In VR, this page is on the Canvas tab.

steps.title: Go in
steps.html:
🔗 First time only: connect Canvas at xr.optimaed.com. See Having trouble in VR? below.

Open the On-Demand app. Click Explore. Type Gallery in Filter environments. Click Optima Gallery, then Begin Solo.

steps.title: Build the hall
steps.html: Put the 5 objects in a row along one wall, with space between them: the textbook, the microphone, the train, the quill and the storybook. Make them all the same size.

steps.title: Take your photo and send it
steps.html:
Open your menu, click Library, then Camera. Fit your whole build in the tablet. Click Take photo.

On the Canvas tab, pick @CANVAS@. Click Choose from My Files, pick your photo, click Use this file, then Submit to Canvas. Look for the green Submitted tag.

🔁 To fix it, send a new photo.

steps.title: Check and leave
steps.html: Press the Meta button, then click Quit. Check that your photo is in the Canvas assignment. Not there? See Having trouble in VR?

extra.html: Put them in time order, from Walls (1871) to Hurston's novel (1937).

vr.full: One photo that shows all five objects in the hall.

studio.title: Leader Memory Match
studio.look: Twelve cards, face down. Six show a leader's name. Six tell what a leader did.
studio.do: Flip two cards. If they match, they stay open.

labels.step: Flip two cards. Find a leader and what they did.

game.miss: Not a match. Remember where they are, and try again.
game.done: All six pairs! Each leader served Florida in a different way.

pairs.b: Started a school with five girls in 1904
pairs.ok: Yes! It grew into Bethune-Cookman University.

pairs.b: Wrote the words to Lift Every Voice and Sing
pairs.ok: Yes! 500 students in Jacksonville sang it first.

pairs.b: Started a union of sleeping car porters
pairs.ok: Yes! In 1937 his union won an agreement with the Pullman Company.

pairs.b: Florida's first Black member of Congress
Wrote Their Eyes Were Watching God
pairs.ok: Yes! She grew up in Eatonville.

pairs.b: Helped thousands of Black Floridians sign up to vote
pairs.ok: Yes! He and Harriette Moore were teachers in Mims.
